records.date_note: Kenya Red Cross posts of 15 March; the school closures happened over the days before.
records.description: The Ngong River burst its banks, cutting off two schools in Mukuru; about nine schools in Nairobi closed. Nairobi recorded 59 mm of rain in the 24 hours to 15 March.

links.title: Kenya – Deadly Floods Strike Again

records.place: Mukuru informal settlements, Embakasi Girls Secondary School

records.date_note: Overnight rain into Wednesday 24 April.
records.description: Flash floods across Nairobi; people were rescued from rooftops in Mathare. Across the city, police counted at least 10 dead, with others missing, and the county governor's office said about 60,000 people were severely affected.
records.reported_by: Police, Nairobi County, Kenya Red Cross

records.date_note: Night of Friday 6 to Saturday 7 March, after heavy rain on 6 March.
records.description: Overnight floods across Nairobi after the Nairobi River burst its banks. Across the city, police first confirmed 10 deaths and 71 vehicles caught by floodwater; later reports put the toll at 23, most recovered from rivers in Starehe and Kamukunji.
records.reported_by: Police, Ministry of Interior, Kenya Red Cross

records.description: An evening downpour flooded roads and estates as the Nairobi and Ngong rivers overflowed. The Kenya Red Cross rescued 11 people from a matatu on Bunyala Road and reported no deaths from this wave.
